full_judgment:
SK Sinha J: These Rules arise out of complaint Case No. 2018 of 1998 pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and therefore, these Rules are disposed of by this judgment. Petitioners sought anticipatory bail and this Court issued a Rule and enlarged them on ad- interim anticipatory bail. This Rule gave rise to Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4042 of 1998. Thereafter, the petitioners moved two applications for quashing the proceedings of the case. Other two Rules were issued pursuant thereto. 

 3. The learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate on examination of the complainant, it is said, issued summons against the petitioners. On perusal of the petitions, we have noticed that the petitioners have not annexed the order of the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate taking cognizance of the offence. Therefore, technically there was no legal proceeding when the applications were moved before the Court. These petitions being not in accordance with law, the Rules issued on those petitions are liable to be discharged on this point alone. When these facts were brought to the notice of the learned Advocate for the petitioners, the petitioner Amal Cabraal file a supplementary affidavit on 27-4-2003 in connection with his Rule being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6948 of 1998 enclosing the order of the learned Magistrate. John Noal has not filed any order of the learned Magistrate. 

 5. In the applications, the petitioners made statements that without using models, Lever Brothers televised advertisement with real life persons for the promotion of its product, which is an innovation, consciously launched in the market on being satisfied that the launching of such advertisement did not violate section 294B of the Penal Code. Petitioners further state that the gifts given to the participants have no bearing nor the same may be deemed by any stretch of imagination as consideration for lying for Lever Brothers products which may be deemed as consideration for the time given by the consumers for their participation in the promotional and advertisement schemes. These statements clearly suggest that the petitioners have admitted the disputed advertisement in question was televised in the Television and over the Radio. These are disputed facts which cannot be decided when exercising a jurisdiction under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. This is a function of the trial Court which would decide appropriately those facts on the basis of the evidence which will be adduced by the parties in the case. 

 7. The offence consists in the publication of such offer does not depend on whether the offers were really carried out or not. The intention of the legislature appears to have been that the public should not be informed of such offers. If offers are such as come within the mischief of section 294B, the offence is completed by publishing them and it does not matter whether the scheme is actually to be an inducement or to merely defraud the public. 

 9. Before the expressions "against any coupon" there is a "comma (,)" between the parts of the sentence and again, another "comma" before the expressions "or by any other device". The legislature consciously used these' commas' as the points that mark discontinuity of the sentence. Similarly, the word 'or' has been used after the "comma". The word "or" in a statute may be read "and" and vice-versa, whenever the change is necessary to effectuate the obvious intention of the legislature. The Court should have recourse to this exceptional rule of construction only when the conversion of the words "or" into "and" one into the other, is necessary to carry into effect the meaning and intention of the legislature. The language of the section 294B does not justify interpretation of the word "or" occurring in the section as "and". The disjunctive "or" used before the expressions "against any coupon, ticket, number or figure", cannot say to be used in the sense of a conjunctive so as to give a correct meaning and the intention of the legislature. The word "against’ ‘has no nexus with the words "or by any other device". These expressions are used in between two "commas" which are so clear, unambiguous and independent to the expression against that the dominant object and spirit of the legislature can be spelt out from the language. If we accept the construction intended to be given by the learned advocate that would give rise to anomaly, which would result in absurdity, which cannot be accepted. The expression "or by any other device" used in the section, according to us, means that any person who offers in connection with any business or sale of any commodity, any prize or reward including the one Lever Brothers had offered to the consumers would come within the mischief of section 294B of the Penal Code. 

 11. In respect of the other Rule, we find that the petitioners are enjoying the privilege of anticipatory bail for more than four years against whom there is no allegation of misuse of privilege of bail. On consideration of the facts of the given case, we are of the view that the petitioners should be allowed to enjoy such privilege till the conclusion of the trial of the case. 

 12. Before parting with the case, we would like to observe that we are compelled to make some observations as the learned Advocates for the petitioners prefer a judgment from us on interpretation of the provisions of law in the facts of the given case. Whatever observations made herein above, shall have no bearing on the merit of the case and the trial Court shall be at liberty to dispose of the case on the basis of the evidence to be adduced by the parties. 

 In the result, the Rules in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 6948 and 5341 of 1998 are discharged and the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4042 of 1998 is made absolute. The stay orders made earlier are hereby vacated.
